subject: dragonfly
pitch: An emperor dragonfly hovering above a pond. A long, slim abdomen in electric blue with black markings down its back, an apple-green thorax, huge wraparound turquoise eyes, and four glassy wings with a fine net of dark veins and a faint golden sheen, held flat and wide. Six thin legs are tucked under it.
reasoning:
I need to write a single TypeScript module using the SDK, but since the reference is partial, I'll stick strictly to documented helpers like createBuilder, joint, chain, sweep, part, stick, membrane, cards, decal, region, lathe, extrude, paint, spots, stripes, countershade, svg, frame, line, rng, and a.

For the dragonfly hovering over the pond, I'm reasoning through realistic scale — an emperor dragonfly's body is roughly 8cm with a 10-11cm wingspan, so I'll keep dimensions close to real life (~0.085m length, ~0.11m wingspan) rather than inflating for visibility. Since it's in flight rather than resting, I'm placing the model's center around y=0.3 to represent hovering height, noting that the "nothing hangs below the floor" rule doesn't apply here since it's airborne.

Now I'm planning the body construction: a head with large bulbous eyes using sphere geometries, a thorax built from scaled spheres to approximate a capsule shape, and attaching eye spheres at the sides in a turquoise color via the part/bone/scale options.

I'm working out how to build the abdomen as a chain of joints running backward from the thorax, considering whether to use varying-radius sweeps or lofted stations versus simpler stacked cylinder segments colored in alternating rings, and figuring out the right joint signature (at, aim, dir, up) to orient each segment correctly along the tail.

Then I'm planning the head joint placement and eye spheres scaled to wrap around the sides, followed by sketching out the abdomen chain's path points with a slight downward dip near the tip, sweeping it with a thin blue tube, and considering how to attach small black marking boxes along the top using the chain's tangent frames via stick placement.

Since I'm uncertain how `parent` and frame offsets actually work in this API, I'll minimize reliance on them by computing the abdomen centreline points myself in an array, then deriving world positions for the black band markings directly from that array rather than trusting frame-offset methods.

For the wings, I'm thinking of using membranes stretched between a leading-edge and trailing-edge point path for each of the four wings, with a pale translucent color, and adding thin sweeps along the edges plus a few cross-sweeps as simple vein details rather than attempting a textured vein pattern.

I'm thinking about rigging the wings as joint chains with a wing role, then moving on to the six tucked legs as thin swept chains with knees and feet. For the body, I'm sketching the thorax as a scaled sphere and the abdomen tapering back with a slight downward droop toward the tip.

Now I'm figuring out the abdomen's centerline curve with decreasing radius toward the tip, electric-blue coloring, and dark dorsal patches placed along the curve, plus small cerci at the tail and large turquoise eyes with a dark head sphere up front.

For the wings, I'm setting up joint chains using the builder's chain function so membranes ride the bones automatically, then adding longitudinal veins as thin sweeps and cross-veins by interpolating points between the leading and trailing edge curves, writing my own vector math helpers to stay within the known SDK methods like part, chain, sweep, and membrane.

Working out the forewing and hindwing leading/trailing edge coordinates with slight sinusoidal bowing, then placing several cross veins at intervals along each wing to create a membrane grid.

Now I'm thinking through colors: glassy blue-white membrane with golden cross veins, a dark pterostigma spot near the forewing tip, and body colors — electric blue abdomen, black accents, apple green thorax, turquoise eyes, black legs.

For legs, I'm planning three per side with hip-knee-tarsus joint chains swept into thin tubes, tucked under the body. I'm realizing each chain likely needs a parent joint since only one root joint is allowed, so I need to pass a parent option when creating these leg chains to avoid a "second root" error.

I'm structuring the skeleton hierarchy with a body root joint, then head, thorax, abdomen, wings, and legs all parented appropriately through the thorax, so the whole creature forms one connected rig that sweeps can ride on.

Now I'm sketching helper utilities for interpolating points and mirroring across the x-axis, then setting up the main module with type definitions and a body centerline, defining the abdomen's curve as a tapering series of points for the chain sweep.

Adding dorsal black marking patches along the abdomen segments plus cerci cones at the tail tip...

For the cerci I'll switch to a swept tube shape per side instead of fighting cone orientation. For the thorax, I'll apply geometry.scale directly to stretch the sphere rather than passing an unsupported scale option, then add thin black dorsal stripe boxes on top and a darker head sphere with scaled eye spheres.

Now I'm setting up the skeleton: a body joint as root, head and thorax joints as children, an abdomen chain tagged as the tail role, and wing chains built from root-mid-tip points along the leading edge so the membrane geometry can sample from them.

For legs I'm adding six simple three-point chains parented to the thorax. For the wings I'm defining parametric curves for leading and trailing edges of the forewing, adjusting the coordinates so the chord and span better match a realistic dragonfly wing shape, using a seeded rng for subtle vein jitter to keep things deterministic.

Now I'm working out the hindwing's leading and trailing edge curves with their own sweep and chord, then placing cross veins, a pterostigma marking, and two longitudinal veins between the edges. Finally I'm building the wing membranes from sampled leading/trailing edge points and mirroring the whole wing setup for the right side.

Setting up cross-vein sweeps, legs, and joint chains...
